solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lie about London's food

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang, London's own street talk, a fib is a 'porky pie', rhyming with lie
a savoury snack of seasoned meat baked in a raised pastry case

explanation.surface: Someone tells a fib about what the capital eats.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang is a London habit of replacing a word with a phrase that rhymes with it; 'porkies' for lies comes from it. A pork pie is also a classic British cold pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: rhyming slang for a fib, and a traditional British meat pastry.

clue.text: Set the level and tried to sell

definitions.meaning: to fix the level of something, as a musical note or a price, is to give it a particular height
a salesperson makes a sales talk to a customer

explanation.surface: Someone fixed a price and then tried to make a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of the verb: fixing a tone or level, and making a sales talk to win a customer.

clue.text: Retrospective discounts for beers at brewing

indicators.note: brewing is the mixing and fermenting of ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub offers money back on the beer being brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing' rearranges BEERS and AT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Money returned after a payment is made, a partial refund given after the event.

clue.text: In Mexico, money protects the origin of tartare sauce

indicators.note: to protect something is to wrap round it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: the peso is the currency of Mexico

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Cash in Mexico supposedly guards a tartare sauce recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' puts the T from 'the origin of tartare' inside PESO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian basil, pine nut and cheese paste served on pasta is a kind of sauce.

clue.text: Terribly overactive with no right being reminiscent

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly messed up, so the letters are jumbled
with no means a letter is taken away from the word

explanation.surface: Someone hyperactive without a right side brings back memories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes R from OVERACTIVE, leaving OVEACTIVE, which 'Terribly' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that calls up memories or feelings is suggestive, bringing to mind past times.

clue.text: Iris maybe making bread

definitions.meaning: an iris is a flowering plant, something that blooms, an example of a flowerer
a large crusty white loaf with diagonal slashes on top

explanation.surface: Iris, perhaps, is baking a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name; it is the flower. A bloomer is a British style of loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a plant that flowers, and a long crusty loaf with slashes on top.

clue.text: House call?

parts.note: not a doctor's visit but the shout of a winning player in the number game also known as House

explanation.walkthrough: 'House call' suggests a doctor's home visit; in the British numbers game also called House or housey-housey, the winner shouts out a word.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a winner in the numbers game, which in Britain is also called House.

clue.text: Arrange duo's roles without a stink

indicators.note: to arrange is to put things in a new order, here the letters

parts.note: the possessive spelt out gives its S as a letter here

explanation.surface: A director recasts the parts of a double act, with no bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' rearranges DUOS and ROLES together.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no smell at all, scentless, free of any whiff.

clue.text: Sugar from whisky like this raised energy

parts.note: malt is short for malt whisky

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted up, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: so can mean in this way, like this
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Sugar extracted from Scotch is somehow turned into energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SO upside down to OS in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A sugar formed when starch is broken down, as in malting grain.

clue.text: Admires pectorals, admitting deference

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the clue words hold the run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone admires a gym-goer's chest muscles with due deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' says the letters run inside 'adm(IRES PECT)orals'.
explanation.definitionFit: Due regard and esteem for someone, synonymous with deference and courtesy.

clue.text: A cost involved over a black pepper sauce

indicators.note: over here means covering or around, one piece set across the other
involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A pepper sauce costs something to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A COST to TASCO, and 'over' puts it round A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot condiment made from fiery red chillies, vinegar and salt.

clue.text: Pasta and beans

definitions.meaning: long thin strips of dough, often eaten in soups
bean is slang for the head, and noodle is too, so both are words for heads

explanation.surface: A menu offers pasta with beans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beans' looks like a food to go with the pasta; it is slang for heads, as in 'use your bean'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: strips of pasta, and slang for heads, matching beans in the same slang sense.

clue.text: A couple of tomatoes added to stew creates an awkward situation

indicators.note: one piece added to another follows it in the answer

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew of meat and vegetables under sliced potato, as in Lancashire hotpot

indicators.note: a couple of letters from the start of the word, the first two

explanation.surface: A cook tips a couple of tomatoes into a stew that turns out awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple of' takes the opening pair of letters of 'tomatoes', and 'added to' sets them after the stew. Lancashire hotpot is a traditional northern English stew of meat under sliced potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a controversial issue nobody wants to handle, a delicate problem.

clue.text: River horse, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals a word as said out loud, matching another in sound

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat mixed with white hairs

explanation.surface: A hippopotamus, or river horse, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River horse' looks like the hippopotamus; it is two parts: the definition and the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A major French river flowing from the Alps through Lyon to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Measures bit of salt eaten by deer

indicators.note: eaten by puts one piece inside the other, as if swallowed

parts.note: does are female deer

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Deer lick at a salt block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten by' puts S, from 'bit of salt', inside DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Quantities of medicine to be taken at one time, measured amounts.

clue.text: Fondly-remembered youth's healthy dishes covering twenty-four hours

definitions.note: the possessive 's reads as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: covering means wrapped round, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: salads are dishes thought of as healthy
a day lasts twenty-four hours

explanation.surface: A young person's nutritious meals take up a whole day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' wraps the dishes round the period of time. The phrase comes from Shakespeare's Cleopatra: 'my salad days, when I was green in judgement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for the carefree, inexperienced time of being young, recalled with affection.

clue.text: Simple mention exposes piece of equipment

indicators.note: exposes means uncovers, revealing letters already held within the clue words

explanation.surface: A plain remark reveals a tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposes' says the letters run inside 's(IMPLE MENT)ion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or utensil, an instrument used for a task.

clue.text: Attendant welcoming a charter for ancestry

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a page is a young attendant
to charter a boat or plane is to hire or rent it

explanation.surface: A steward greets a charter flight's passengers with talk of family trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' has the attendant take in A plus the word for hire, just after his opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lineage and origins, who one's mother and father and forebears were.

clue.text: Live in reduced surroundings? It's hardly worth considering

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another, with surroundings showing the outer one encloses it

parts.note: something reduced is made smaller
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Downsizing your home is a trifling matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the work; 'surroundings' only confirms that the reduced word encloses the living. Small beer was originally weak ale, hence something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for something trivial or unimportant, originally weak ale of little strength.

clue.text: Exclude American during budget

indicators.note: during means within a period, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: to budget is to plan how to spend

explanation.surface: An American is left out of budget discussions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' sets the American within the budget word; 'Exclude' is meant in the sense of suspending a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone for a time, as a pupil from school, is to exclude them.

clue.text: Funny thinking heralded by the first of April

indicators.note: heralded by means preceded by, so the other piece comes first
the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: musing is thinking or reflecting

explanation.surface: A thought on April Fools' Day turns out funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heralded by' puts A, 'the first of April', before MUSING. The first of April, April Fools' Day, adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing laughter or entertainment, a synonym of humorous.

clue.text: Fool — going back to take in a line dance

indicators.note: to take in is to absorb or enclose, so one piece goes inside
going back means read in reverse order

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A clown goes back to join a line dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' reverses ASS to SSA, and 'to take in' puts A and L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Latin American dance, also the music it is danced to.

clue.text: Flipping Christmas at home, initially eating like a lion

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Noel is a word for Christmas
in means at home

indicators.note: initially means at the start, taking the opening letter

explanation.surface: Somebody at home at Christmas eats like a lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' turns NOEL into LEON. 'Flipping' also reads as a mild British expletive.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or resembling the big maned cat, as in a mane of hair.

clue.text: Lined up for an attack, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as told or spoken, a match in sound

parts.note: a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: Troops line up for an assault, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lined up for an attack' reads as one military phrase; 'Lined up' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in order, drawn up in ranks, as troops are.

clue.text: Military unit gets one for a creature from the deep

indicators.note: one is I and a is A, so the A is swapped for an I

parts.note: a squad is a small military unit

explanation.surface: A platoon catches something from the ocean depths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is I, the Roman numeral, which replaces the A of SQUAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-armed sea mollusc, a cephalopod living in deep water.

clue.text: Nothing in beer — and no one runs for wine

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
nothing is zero, shaped like O
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A drinker swaps beer for wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the nothing inside the beer; 'and' and 'for' are just joining words around the rest of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A red grape variety from Burgundy, and the wine made from it.

clue.text: Journalists do some weightlifting

definitions.meaning: the news media as a body, reporters collectively
to push a weight up from the chest, as in a bench lift

explanation.surface: Reporters spend time at the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the newspaper world collectively, and pushing a weight upwards.

clue.text: Slim girl's first obsession

parts.note: slim means thin

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A slender girl's main fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes G from 'girl's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation, as in 'he has a thing about trains', a preoccupation.

clue.text: Go and live abroad with no golf, in Dubai for example

indicators.note: with no means a letter is removed

parts.note: to emigrate is to leave home to live in another country
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Moving abroad without golf to the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes G from EMIGRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the seven states ruled by an emir in the UAE, an example of the type.

clue.text: Identification required in a town generates sarcasm

indicators.note: required in means needed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Being asked for papers in town makes people sarcastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required in' slots the identification into the town just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness or bitterness of tone, a cutting quality like sarcasm.

clue.text: Takes in set involved in excavations

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: digs are archaeological excavations

indicators.note: involved means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An archaeologist absorbs a whole set of finds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns the word set into EST, and 'in' lodges that inside the word for excavations.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb food or information, synonymous with taking in.

clue.text: Boffin becoming chief of hen production

parts.note: eggs are what hens produce
a head is a chief

explanation.surface: A scientist is promoted to run the hen farm.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'chief of hen production' as HEAD of EGG, so EGG comes first. Boffin is British slang for a scientist or brainy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an intellectual or very clever person, a highbrow.
